disease_tomato_late_blight_desc: Late blight is a destructive disease attacking tomatoes and potatoes. It is caused by the oomycete Phytophthora infestans, which thrives in cool, wet weather.
disease_tomato_late_blight_bio_1: Apply bio-fungicides containing Bacillus subtilis to suppress pathogen expansion.
disease_tomato_late_blight_bio_2: Improve soil aeration and apply compost tea to enhance beneficial microbial activity.
disease_tomato_late_blight_chem_1: Apply copper-based fungicides immediately to protect uninfected leaves.
disease_tomato_late_blight_chem_2: Use chlorothalonil or mancozeb as protective sprays.
disease_tomato_late_blight_prev_1: Rotate crops annually; do not plant tomatoes near potatoes.
disease_tomato_late_blight_prev_2: Provide drip irrigation to keep foliage dry.
disease_tomato_late_blight_prev_3: Ensure wide spacing between plants for adequate airflow.
disease_tomato_late_blight_prev_4: Prune and destroy infected leaves immediately. Do not compost infected plant debris.
disease_tomato_leaf_mold_desc: Leaf mold is a fungal disease that thrives in high humidity and moderate temperatures, causing yellow spots on leaf tops and velvet-like mold underneath.
disease_tomato_leaf_mold_bio_1: Spray neem oil solution to control early spread.
disease_tomato_leaf_mold_chem_1: Apply sulfur-based sprays or systemic fungicides.
disease_tomato_leaf_mold_prev_1: Maintain humidity levels below 85% in greenhouses.
disease_tomato_leaf_mold_prev_2: Ensure ventilation and plant resistant tomato varieties.
disease_healthy_plant_desc: No disease detected. Plant appears healthy!
disease_healthy_plant_prev_1: Keep doing what you are doing. Maintain regular watering and fertilization schedules.
disease_healthy_plant_prev_2: Ensure crop rotation and sanitization of tools between harvests.
